gap: No result ChatGPT got states that an HDBaseT link is limited to 10.2 Gbps, so a 4K60 4:4:4 signal (an 18 Gbps feed) has to be compressed to cross it. OREI still calls its UHD14-EXB400-K 'uncompressed' at 394 ft for 4K60 4:4:4. AV Access rates its own 18 Gbps HDBaseT extender at only 131 ft for that same signal.
standout_why: I compared against the two cited OREI support articles (UHD12-EX115-K and UHD14-EXB400-K) and the other OREI support pages in the results. They give each product's distance at each resolution and say '18Gbps'. None of them mentions HDBaseT's 10.2 Gbps limit or compression, and none gives another maker's 4K60 4:4:4 distance to compare with. So the shopper sees 394 ft and 115 ft both labelled '4K60 4:4:4, 18 Gbps', with nothing to show the two figures can't be measured on the same basis.
decides: ChatGPT's 'best for long distances' pick (OREI UHD14-EXB400-K, 394 ft at 4K60) is the figure that conflicts with the 10.2 Gbps HDBaseT limit and with AV Access's 131 ft rating for 4K60 4:4:4. It is also listed as 'Unavailable' on orei.com today. For full 4K60 4:4:4/HDR, the safe way to compare is each maker's own 4K60 distance figure: about 115 ft (OREI UHD12-EX115-K), 131 ft (AV Access over Cat6a/7) and 196 ft (J-Tech, chroma not stated). A run longer than that should be treated as 1080p, or as possibly compressed 4K, until the maker says otherwise. The finding supports the OREI 1x2 for runs under 115 ft and makes the long-distance pick doubtful.

findings.note: Installation's wording: 'despite HDBaseT's 10.2Gbps bandwidth limitation, AVLC can pass the 18Gbps data feeds ... up to and including 4K@60Hz (4:4:4, 8-bit)' by compressing them. This is a 2018 trade-press report about one vendor's compression; it is not the HDBaseT Alliance's own spec text.
